policy_title: Reform Private Rented Sector Regulation and End Leasehold
stated: Labour will overhaul regulation of the private rented sector, immediately abolishing Section 21 'no fault' evictions, preventing exploitation and discrimination against renters, empowering them to challenge unreasonable rent increases, and extending 'Awaab’s Law' to the private sector. The party will also end the feudal leasehold system by enacting Law Commission proposals on enfranchisement, right to manage, and commonhold. They will ban new leasehold flats, make commonhold the default, tackle ground rent charges, and address 'fleecehold' private housing estates and unfair maintenance costs.

source.quote: Labour will legislate where the Conservatives have failed, overhauling the regulation of the private rented sector. We will immediately abolish Section 21 ‘no fault’ evictions, prevent private renters being exploited and discriminated against, empower them to challenge unreasonable rent increases, and take steps to decisively raise standards, including extending ‘Awaab’s Law’ to the private sector. Labour will act where the Conservatives have failed and finally bring the feudal leasehold system to an end. We will enact the package of Law Commission proposals on leasehold enfranchisement, right to manage and commonhold. We will take further steps to ban new leasehold flats and ensure commonhold is the default tenure. We will tackle unregulated and unaffordable ground rent charges. We will act to bring the injustice of ‘fleecehold’ private housing estates and unfair maintenance costs to an end.

bearing_set.reason: Abolishing S21, empowering rent-increase challenges, extending Awaab's Law, and leasehold/ground-rent reform all directly affect security of tenure, rent affordability, and housing quality — core O1 indicators.

Explicit anti-discrimination protections for renters (e.g. against benefit-claimant or family-status discrimination) and leasehold enfranchisement rights are genuine equal-treatment and legal-rights issues within O9's strict scope.

Abolishing ground rents and 'fleecehold' charges ends ongoing wealth transfers from ordinary leaseholders to large freeholders and managing agents; this is a concrete redistribution mechanism that plausibly narrows the rich-poor gap in housing wealth, moving the O14 indicator.

membership_note: The policy's primary locus is housing tenure reform (O1), with genuine secondary bearings on anti-discrimination (O9) and wealth redistribution via leasehold abolition (O14). No material bearing on O10 (standard property-market regulation does not rise to state coercion of landlords) or O13 (supply-side effects are contested and too indirect to assign mechanistically).
